answer: An agent marketplace weights governance votes by tokens locked for 90 days, rather than by account count. A thousand identities sharing one stake get the same total voting power as one identity. Each proposal thread makes this rule visible: even at the zenith of its activity, a swarm gains nothing from headcount. Cheap majority control is a fable; an attacker must acquire and immobilize enough tokens to outweigh honest voters, bearing price risk throughout the lock.
